questions.q: What did David do early in the morning before the sun was up?
choices: Searched the chests for his father's letters
Walked to the village to buy some bread
Bathed in a deep pool in the burn
Climbed the stair-tower again to look around
questions.evidence: had a plunge in a deep whirling pool

questions.q: How did David feel as he sat by the fire thinking about his uncle that morning?
choices: Terrified and ready to run straight back home
Full of conceit, sure he could get the upper hand
Sorry for his old uncle and wishing to forgive him
Bored and hoping something exciting would happen

questions.q: David says the fire showed him "never a ship, never a seaman with a hairy cap." What does this hint at?
choices: David is dreaming about the ships he saw near Edinburgh
David has always wanted to become a sailor and see the whole world
Troubles with ships and seamen are coming that he did not foresee
The warlock of Essendean has put a spell on the kitchen fire
questions.evidence: the least sign of all those tribulations that were ripe to fall on me

questions.q: What interrupted David just as his uncle was trying to think up a lie at breakfast?
choices: A clap of thunder
A scream from upstairs
A knock at the door
A horse in the yard
questions.evidence: we were interrupted by a knocking at the door

questions.q: What did the boy in sea-clothes do as soon as he saw David?
choices: Handed him a letter and ran off at once
Asked him for a coin to buy food
Danced some steps of the sea-hornpipe
Saluted him like a soldier on parade
questions.evidence: he began to dance some steps of the sea-hornpipe

questions.q: What did David notice in the cabin-boy's face despite his cheerful dancing?
choices: A proud look of a ship's captain
A cruel smile like a wicked man's
A bored look as if half asleep
A look between tears and laughter
questions.evidence: a look between tears and laughter

questions.q: Who wrote the letter that the cabin-boy brought?
choices: Mr. Rankeillor, the lawyer and factor
Mr. Campbell, the minister of Essendean
Mr. Shuan, the mate of the trading brig
Elias Hoseason, captain of the Covenant

questions.q: Where was Captain Hoseason staying when he wrote the letter?
choices: With Mr. Rankeillor in his house in town
In a lodging house near Edinburgh castle
Aboard a ship docked at the port of Leith
At the Hawes Inn at the Queen's Ferry
questions.evidence: The Hawes Inn, at the Queen's Ferry

questions.q: Uncle Ebenezer says David would be "swier" to believe him on his word. Using the note in the text, what does "swier" mean?
choices: Unwilling
Afraid
Eager
Proud

questions.q: Whom did Uncle Ebenezer promise they could visit after seeing the captain?
choices: Jennet Clouston, to make her stop her cursing
Mr. Rankeillor, the lawyer who knew David's father
A banker in Edinburgh who kept the family money
The minister of Cramond, to arrange David's schooling
questions.evidence: we can jog on to the lawyer, Mr. Rankeillor's

questions.q: Why did David agree to go with his uncle to the Ferry?
choices: He thought a busy shipping place would be safe, and he wanted to see ships
He hoped to find a ship that would carry him home to Essendean
He wanted to tell the ship's captain about his uncle's attempt to kill him
He believed his uncle had truly changed and could now be trusted
questions.evidence: where my uncle durst attempt no violence

questions.q: What was strange about the weather on the walk, though it was June?
choices: It snowed heavily the whole way there
A thick fog hid the road completely
It was so hot that they had to rest often
It was so cold that it felt like winter
questions.evidence: the time might have been winter

choices: Shuan
Riach
Hoseason
Ransome
questions.evidence: He told me his name was Ransome

questions.q: Why did David pity the cabin-boy rather than believe his boasts of wicked deeds?
choices: David had heard the very same stories from Mr. Campbell
The boy was much too young to have been at sea for so many years
The boy admitted at once that he had made up every word
The stories were unlikely and told with a weak, crazy swagger
questions.evidence: such a weak and crazy swagger in the delivery

questions.q: What did the cabin-boy show David on his leg?
choices: A scar from a fall on the deck
A raw red wound made by Mr. Shuan
A tattoo of the brig Covenant
A bite from a dog in the harbour
questions.evidence: a great, raw, red wound that made my blood run cold

questions.q: The boy said the twenty-pounders included innocents who were "kidnapped or trepanned." What does "trepanned" mean here?
choices: Sent home to their families
Paid well for working at sea
Taught to sail and steer a ship
Tricked or taken away by force

questions.q: What was the building at the end of the pier at the Queen's Ferry?
choices: A ruined castle
A customs house
The Hawes Inn
The parish kirk
questions.evidence: I could see the building which they called the Hawes Inn

questions.q: What did David tell his uncle after they looked down on the Covenant from the hill?
choices: That nothing would bring him on board that ship
That he was far too cold and wished to go home
That he had decided to become a cabin-boy
That he wanted to meet the captain right away
questions.evidence: there's nothing that will bring me on board that Covenant

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: David meeting the lawyer Mr. Rankeillor and learning of his inheritance
David forcing his uncle to explain the truth about his father and the house
David walking to the Queen's Ferry and learning how cruel life on the Covenant is
David running away from Shaws by night and finding work on a ship
questions.evidence: the brig Covenant (for all her pious name) was little better than a hell upon the seas
